record.title: Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses
record.summary: Voluntary guidance that helps businesses, including sole traders, non-profits and individual professionals, use and develop AI systems in a trustworthy way, in line with the OECD AI principles and New Zealand's proportionate, risk-based approach to AI agreed by Cabinet. It covers governance and accountability, legal compliance, risk management, procurement, cybersecurity, privacy, transparency (including labelling AI-generated content), data, model efficacy and human-in-the-loop decision-making, and names risks to cybersecurity, privacy, human rights, workplace culture, the environment, intellectual property and physical safety.
record.notes: Published in July 2025 as the companion to New Zealand's AI strategy (NZ-02). Developed by MBIE with the Government Chief Digital Office and other government agencies, in consultation with members of the AI Forum's Executive Council and Governance Working Group. It is part of a wider suite of responsible AI guidance that includes the Responsible AI Guidance for the Public Service: GenAI, published by the Government Chief Digital Office in the Department of Internal Affairs. A Quickstart Guide for Business Users is published separately.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: every stored copy of the MBIE guidance page and of the strategy page (11 and 17 Oct 2026, also with the browser retry) is a JavaScript bot-check page of the site's web application firewall (Incapsula). The guidance itself was stored in this run as a 43-page PDF from mbie.govt.nz; it confirms the title, July 2025, its voluntary nature, MBIE as author with the Government Chief Digital Office, the AI Forum's role, the risk-based approach and the content areas. MBIE's news release requested in this run could not be stored. Version 1 took July 2025 from the strategy page, which presents the two together; the PDF shows the date itself.
